questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was already quite familiar with my study destination and knew a few people in the city. This, for me, was quite important.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The contact to my host university was very good during the whole stay. Before, as well as during the stay, my host university regularly sent me informations via email – about course registration, student advising, credits, events, etc. I also always received a quick response via email when reaching out to my Erasmus coordinator at my host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinator met us in person on the first orientation day. We also got to meet with a student from our specific field of study who showed us campus and gave us their contact informations as well as recommendations for the university and for the city. That was all very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing via WG-Gesucht. I send messages to a lot (!) of people and eventually found an apartment. I don't know if I would necessarily recommend the site – it worked for me in the end, but I think it was mostly a matter of luck.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed living off campus. Studying abroad is intense – you meet so many new people all the time, you speak a language that is not your mother tongue, maybe you are learning a new language, you go to a lot of social events, etc. So living off campus for me was a nice way to get a break from all of that once in a while.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the student accommodations offered very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can register online, or you can simply show up in the course on the first day and ask the professor if you can join the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: On the introduction day, all exchange students received informations about course registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I more or less got accepted to all the courses I had wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The first two weeks of every semester is "shopping week", meaning that you can go to as many courses you want to see how you like it. After two weeks you decide which courses you would like to do. My advice would be to use those two shopping weeks – it is a good way to get an idea of the professor and the type of class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses were generally high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less people were in the courses at my host university compared to the courses I did at UCPH. This meant that I got to participate way more actively which was very nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Simone de Beauvoir, Introduction to Feminist Philosophy, Saidiya Hartman: Scenes of Subjection, Re-thinking Translation, Law and Literature, Introduction to Cultural Studies: Philosophy of the Bedroom.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: The Second Sex, Kierkegaard, Pop-Medievalism.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found the courses in the philosophy department very nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sport, talks, readings, city tours.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I strongly recommend participating in the social activities on the introduction days. I made most of my friends during those days.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I can recommend going to the many lakes in and around Berlin. Krumme Lanke is only a few stations away from the university. I can also recommend getting a museum card which allows you to enter all of the Staatliche Museen. I can recommend the many markets, Mauerpark, Boxhagener, Bergmankiez, the Turkish market at Maybachufer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the social activities during the introduction days. Search for a language tandem partner.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You are not alone – you can always seek help at the university! Discover the cute and lively cafés and courtyards on campus. Enjoy your stay – FUB is great!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Reaching the end of my second semester, I feel sincerely happy and proud that I dared throwing myself into this experience. I feel personally and academically inspired and motivated – and I believe the main reason for this is the lovely and inspiring people I have met along the way, on and off campus.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
